reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer 2 identified the new OMIEC-based THz device and its use on rigid and flexible substrates; the final paper documents the THz implementation and fully direct-written architecture in P:S-c143fbedb2c4768cf91c and P:S-0b3748ef1910545f7f5f.

Reviewer 2 noted the accessible, low-temperature-compatible deposition approach; the final paper describes direct writing, low-temperature processing, and plastic-substrate compatibility in P:S-d2891937a6b639b7c914 and P:S-0b3748ef1910545f7f5f.

Reviewer 2 characterized the use of OMIECs for THz applications as a first; the final paper states that no THz metadevice based on organic electronic materials had been proposed and presents the OMIEC tuning-layer contribution in P:S-256e571c564113650ef4 and P:S-c143fbedb2c4768cf91c.

Reviewer 2 questioned why a mixed conductor is needed or preferable to an organic semiconductor. The final paper supports a residual scope limit: it reports limited OMIEC mobility relative to inorganic and 2D materials and identifies fundamental transport questions as open in P:S-aedb3027520e6f882a22.

Reviewer 1 requested a balanced lifecycle assessment behind environmental framing. The final paper adds process-level sustainability rationale in P:S-d2891937a6b639b7c914 and presents environmental improvements as prospective in P:S-aedb3027520e6f882a22, leaving lifecycle performance unquantified.

Reviewer 1 raised mass-scale consistency and reliability concerns. The final paper describes the process as scalable in principle and its reliability advantages as potential in P:S-5bbf368dbd8f6b5b9f8e, rather than providing mass-scale reliability evidence.

Reviewer 2 found the presentation insufficiently general and accessible, and later noted that key response details had not entered the manuscript. The final paper retains high-level open transport and device-speed statements in P:S-aedb3027520e6f882a22 and P:S-6a3970b842bfdac50542, supporting a remaining accessibility limitation.

Reviewer 1 asked about integration with existing high-frequency devices and systems. The final paper explicitly calls for characterization and optimization of modulation speed to establish relevance for wireless communications in P:S-6a3970b842bfdac50542.

Reviewer 1 asked whether Drude-Smith can capture the diverse scattering and degradation processes in semiconducting polymers. The final paper states that the microscopic origin of the localization parameter and localized carriers remains open in P:S-c74740c9020b8512244a and P:S-aedb3027520e6f882a22.

Reviewer 2 objected to an overly broad first-inkjet-printing formulation. The author response states that the wording was removed; the final paper describes p(g2T-TT) deposition by inkjet printing without that priority wording in P:S-a391a0e59ebf9788755a.

Reviewer 2 requested a more rigorous explanation of organic-material limitations at high frequency. The final paper attributes the limitation to carrier mobility, charge injection, and switching speed in P:S-a391a0e59ebf9788755a.

Reviewer 2 identified an unlabeled feature in Fig. 2a and reiterated the clarity concern in round 2. The final Fig. 2 caption identifies the three-electrode device in P:S-2e9598497e4487feb1fc, and the figure text labels the impinging and transmitted THz beams in P:S-2b5f79438fd5f5b3ee9a.

Reviewer 2 requested clearer distinction between metastructure and metadevice terminology. The response reports terminology changes, while the final paper uses metadevice architecture and metasurface terminology in P:S-6b6700711d8cccbbf1d4 and P:S-2e9598497e4487feb1fc.

Reviewer 2 requested clarification of the three-electrode device, gate voltage, and diagram correspondence. The final text explains the OECT and two-electrode configurations and their respective conductivity measurements in P:S-2b6d70bba802e0450866.

limiting_points.suggested_action: State more directly how OMIEC-specific volumetric charge modulation compares with conventional organic-semiconductor tuning under matched device conditions.
limiting_points.text: The novelty is a proof-of-principle OMIEC integration; the final paper still identifies limited carrier mobility and unresolved transport questions, so its comparative advantage over other organic tuners remains incompletely established.

supporting_points.text: The work extends organic mixed ion-electron conductors to electrically reconfigurable THz metadevices, a setting the paper identifies as previously lacking an organic-electronic implementation.

questions.suggested_action: Quantify switching speed and identify the device and materials parameters that govern integration into representative high-frequency systems.
questions.text: What modulation-speed limits and integration constraints govern use of these metadevices in existing high-frequency systems, particularly wireless applications?

questions.suggested_action: Test the transport interpretation with complementary structural, electrical, and spectroscopic measurements across materials and gating conditions.
questions.text: Which microscopic scattering, trapping, structural, and degradation processes determine the Drude-Smith localization parameter and the associated screening response?

strengths.text: The paper demonstrates an OMIEC-tuned THz metadevice and carries the implementation through both conventional and fully direct-written devices on rigid and flexible substrates.
The direct-writing route combines inkjet printing and femtosecond laser ablation with low-temperature-compatible processing and plastic-substrate compatibility.

summary.text: This study applies an organic mixed ion-electron conductor as an electrically controlled tuning layer for THz metasurfaces, including fully direct-written devices on rigid and flexible substrates. The contribution is specific and supported by measured modulation, while the final paper leaves transport interpretation, modulation-speed relevance, lifecycle claims, scale-up reliability, and some broader explanatory context as residual limits.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Separate demonstrated process attributes from lifecycle conclusions and provide, or explicitly delimit the absence of, lifecycle assessment.
weaknesses.text: Environmental benefits are presented through process attributes and prospective recycling or solvent routes, without a balanced quantitative lifecycle assessment.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Add evidence or clearly bounded discussion of yield, uniformity, and reliability for larger-area or scaled manufacturing.
weaknesses.text: Mass-manufacturing feasibility and process reliability are described as potential or in-principle outcomes rather than demonstrated under scaled production conditions.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Bring the key practical and mechanistic explanations needed by non-specialists into the main text, with clear scope limits.
weaknesses.text: The final manuscript retains high-level statements about open transport and speed questions, while key explanatory detail remains insufficiently developed for a broad audience.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The contested first-inkjet-printing priority wording is absent from the final text.
The final introduction replaces the criticized preconception framing with a mobility, injection, and switching-speed explanation.
The Fig. 2 device and THz-beam annotations are identified in the final caption and figure text.
The final manuscript uses metasurface and metadevice architecture terminology consistently enough to resolve the terminology request.
The final text explains the three-terminal OECT and grounded two-electrode configurations and connects them to the reported measurements.
